note: Every name carries a signed edge_score on -100..+100. There is no call and no threshold: rank on edge_score and cut wherever you like afterwards, which is what makes the ranking question answerable at every k.

findings.finding: UNFI's largest customer decelerated inside UNFI's Q4 window: Amazon's 'Physical stores' net sales (mostly Whole Foods) grew 3.6% YoY in Q2 2026 ($5,794mm vs $5,595mm) versus 4.6% in Q1 2026 ($5,785mm vs $5,533mm) — and the Q2 2025 base was itself the quarter of the June 2025 UNFI cyber outage that produced documented Whole Foods out-of-stocks, so the true underlying deceleration is worse than 100bp.
findings.adversary_note: The facts check out exactly and the base-quarter logic is sound, but the size does not reach the print. Amazon Q2 2026 Physical stores was $5,794mm vs $5,595mm (+3.56%) and Q1 2026 was $5,785mm vs $5,533mm (+4.55%) -- so the deceleration is real, and it was visible in Amazon's OWN rounded labels, which went from '5%' in the Q1 release to '4%' in the Q2 release, published 2026-07-30 in the document every Amazon analyst reads and tracked publicly as a series on Statista. Three problems. (1) 'Physical stores' is not Whole Foods: it bundles Amazon Fresh and Amazon Go, and it is retail sell-through, not UNFI's wholesale shipments into the account. (2) Amazon's Apr-Jun quarter covers only two of the three months in UNFI's 13 weeks to 2026-08-01. (3) The arithmetic: 100bp on a customer worth ~20-22% of UNFI net sales is ~20bp of UNFI revenue, about $15mm on a $7.6bn quarter, and at UNFI's ~2.2% adjusted EBITDA margin that is a rounding error against a $0.62 EPS bar. Worse for the hunter, the conclusion it supports -- soft top line -- is already marked: UNFI's revenue line is dominated by its own deliberate network-optimization exits and a single-customer project unwind that management said on 2026-06-09 will 'fully cycle in the third quarter of fiscal 2027', the June print missed revenue by ~$236mm and cost 10.3%, and Q4 consensus revenue of $7.6bn already sits at the very floor of the band implied by guidance (which is UNFI-h2#2's own finding). The sell-side has already taken revenue to the bottom; this datum tells it to do what it has done.

findings.finding: The initial FY2027 guidance at this print will be delivered by a CFO who started on 2026-08-10 — day 29 of his tenure and nine days after the fiscal year closed — as the fifth element of an eight-week C-suite reshuffle that includes an entirely unannounced departure: Matthew Echols ceased serving as Chief Corporate Affairs Officer effective 2026-08-24, disclosed only in an exit Form 4 filed 2026-08-27 with no press release and no 8-K.
findings.adversary_note: This is two facts welded together and they price completely differently. The reshuffle itself is not obscure at all: the 8-K (report date 2026-07-07) came with a Businesswire press release on 2026-07-09 -- 'United Natural Foods Announces Leadership Updates to Accelerate Value Creation Strategy' -- naming Luchini CFO effective 2026-08-10, Tarditi to President/COO, Martin to Chief Commercial Officer and Bushway's exit, and it was picked up by TipRanks, The Shelby Report, Supermarket News, Progressive Grocer, Mass Market Retailers, Abasto and Distribution Strategy Group inside 48 hours. Nobody discovers on 2026-09-04 that UNFI has a five-week-old CFO. The Echols Form 4 I concede: I searched and found no press release, no Item 5.02, no trade-press item, and the filing itself does carry the remark that he ceased to be Chief Corporate Affairs Officer effective 2026-08-24. But that is a communications and public-affairs role with no P&L line and no guidance role -- its earnings content is approximately zero, and it is doing all the work of making this finding look unpublished. Strip it out and what remains is 'a new CFO may sandbag his first guide', which is one of the most widely rehearsed patterns in the market and whose trigger date has been public for eight weeks. The 'day 29' framing is a re-description of a known start date, not a new fact.

findings.finding: UNFI's ~$330mm FY2026 free cash flow guide contains at least $40mm of one-off cyber insurance cash already banked through Q3 ($20mm in Q3 alone, 'included within Operating expenses'), which management itself strips out of adjusted EBITDA via a ($18mm) YTD 'Cybersecurity incident' reconciliation line — while the December 2025 framework anchors FCF at only '~$300 million annually from fiscal 2026 to fiscal 2028'.
findings.adversary_note: The facts are right but the hunter has double-counted the benefit, and every component comes from two documents the company published itself and the hunter itself cites. Verified from the Q3 FY26 release: '$20 million and $40 million of insurance recoveries' in Q3 and YTD, 'included within Operating expenses', the ~$330mm FCF guide, and the cybersecurity reconciliation. But the same release states the $40mm of recoveries is offset by '$22 million of costs and charges' -- which is precisely why the reconciliation line is ($18mm) and not ($40mm). So the one-off flattering FY26 free cash flow is ~$18mm net, roughly 5.5% of the $330mm guide, not the 'at least $40mm' the finding asserts. Against the December 2025 framework, the FY26 guide is $30mm above the ~$300mm anchor and ~$18mm of that is the net cyber item -- a real quality-of-cash-flow point, but worth well under 1% of a $2.67bn market cap. And the framework itself is the problem for the finding: 'Approximately $300 million annually from fiscal 2026 to fiscal 2028' is *published guidance* from the 2025-12-10 investor day press release, so if UNFI guides FY27 FCF to ~$300mm on 2026-09-08 that is management restating its own plan on schedule, which is the definition of already priced. The finding is only news if the market thought $330mm was the new run rate, and the company's own published framework says otherwise.

findings.finding: Nine days after the -10.3% Q3 reaction, UNFI's lenders repriced its term loan 75bp tighter — Amendment No. 5, dated 2026-06-18, cut the SOFR margin from 4.75% to 4.00% on ~$371mm outstanding with 'all of the other material terms' unchanged, i.e. no covenant relief was needed.
findings.adversary_note: This one is in the wire copy and it is arithmetically trivial. Amendment No. 5 was 8-K'd and then written up on the day by Investing.com, TradingView, TipRanks and StockTitan, all of which carried the exact detail the finding leads with -- SOFR margin 4.75% to 4.00% on approximately $371mm, other material terms unchanged. Size: 75bp on $371mm is $2.78mm a year pretax, call it $2.1mm after tax, which on 60.7mm shares outstanding is about $0.035 of annual EPS and under a cent in the quarter being reported. Against a stock at $43.94 with a 12.02% implied move that is roughly a tenth of a point of value, not a thesis. The 'no covenant relief was needed' inference is also weaker than it reads: 2026 has been a broad repricing market and a lender repricing a $371mm first-lien tranche at 2.5x net leverage tells you about loan-market technicals as much as about UNFI. Decisively, the price did not agree that this mattered: the amendment was dated 2026-06-18 and disclosed 2026-06-22, and UNFI has since gone from $47.90 on 2026-08-13 to $43.94, with a -6.6% 20-day run-up. A credit-confidence signal that leaves no trace in the equity for eleven weeks is not an unpriced 12%-move catalyst.

findings.finding: US Foods' CFO said on 2026-08-13 that his fuel surcharge recovery rate ran "more like 70% for the quarter" versus "our typical 30%, 40%", turning an expected 2% fuel headwind into "less than half of that", explicitly because high diesel "triggered additional customer surcharges that normally only activate at elevated price levels" - the same tiered-surcharge mechanism UNFI described on 2026-06-09 as "contractual protection to share some of the fuel pressures with our customers", in a quarter that overlaps UNFI's 13 weeks to 2026-08-01.
findings.adversary_note: I checked the transcript and the quotes are exact -- CFO Dirk Locascio, recovery 'more like 70% for the quarter' against 'our typical 30%, 40%', an expected 'about a 2% headwind from fuel' coming in at 'less than half of that', explicitly because surcharges for larger customers that only activate at elevated prices went into effect. UNFI's own 2026-06-09 language is also exact: hedging, 'contractual protection to share some of the fuel pressures with our customers', route optimisation. So the mechanism is real and I have not found the read-across written down for UNFI anywhere. That is a genuine concession. The case against it is about transfer and about how much room is left. Transfer: US Foods is broadline foodservice, small drop sizes, a fragmented restaurant base and its own negotiated surcharge tables; UNFI is grocery wholesale whose single largest customer is ~20-22% of net sales and has more negotiating leverage than any USFD account, and UNFI's own word is 'some', not 'most'. Overlap: USFD's quarter is Apr-Jun, UNFI's is 3 May to 1 Aug, and diesel collapsed to $4.58 on 2026-07-06 before rebounding through July -- so the very tiers that fired in May and June may have deactivated in the month USFD does not cover. Room left: UNFI told the market on 2026-06-09 that incremental fuel and transportation costs were already embedded in Q4 guidance, the 2026-09-03 preview repeats it, and Q4 consensus EPS of $0.62 against Q3's $0.77 actual already books a sharp sequential step down that is largely fuel. The upside is therefore against a bar that has already been lowered. What keeps my number low anyway is that the tape moved the other way: UNFI was $47.90 on 2026-08-13, the day of the USFD call, and is $43.94 now -- the market spent those three weeks pricing fuel pain, not surcharge relief.

findings.finding: UNFI's 2022 Repurchase Program - $200m authorised 2022-09-21 for a four-year term, so its term runs out this month - still had approximately $109m unused as of 2026-05-02, equal to about 4.2% of the $2.6bn market cap, while net leverage is already at 2.5x heading to ~2.3x against a stated <=2.5x-by-FY26 target and the last buys were struck at $33.66 (Q2) versus $43.94 spot.
findings.adversary_note: The core mechanic checks out and the precedent is real, which is why my number is not higher: the $200mm programme was approved 2022-09-21 'over four years', so it does lapse this month, and it was itself announced alongside the Q4 FY2022 print on 2022-09-27 -- so a Q4 print is exactly where UNFI re-ups. The $109mm is also credible: $138mm remained at FY23 year end and FY26 year-to-date buybacks were about $38mm at an average of $37.88 per the Q3 call, leaving roughly $100mm. Three things cut it down. First, the theme is already on the record: management said on the 2026-06-09 call it would 'continue to evaluate further opportunistic repurchases as we reinvest in our business and reduce leverage', so buyback capacity is not a discovery. Second, one of the finding's specifics is wrong -- the last buys were not 'struck at $33.66 (Q2)'. The Q3 10-Q shows 0.1mm shares for $4mm in the third quarter, about $40 a share, and the call gives a $37.88 year-to-date average, so buying continued into Q3 well above $33.66, which weakens the 'they only buy when it is cheap, so $43.94 is above their revealed bid' subtext considerably. Third, an authorisation is not a purchase: a board can let a term lapse silently, and UNFI's stated capital priority is deleveraging toward and through 2.5x. Against a name with a 12.02% implied move driven by the first FY27 guide, a new authorisation is a second-order headline.

findings.finding: The Q4 bar the wire will print at 6:30am - $7.6bn revenue, $0.62 adjusted EPS - is asymmetric against UNFI's own narrowed FY26 guide: $31.1-31.3bn sales less $23.51bn of 39-week actuals implies Q4 sales of $7.59-7.79bn, so $7.6bn sits at the floor of the guided band, whereas $2.40-2.60 adjusted EPS less $1.95 YTD implies Q4 of $0.45-0.65 and $0.62 sits at the ~85th percentile.
findings.adversary_note: Every input verifies and the arithmetic is correct -- FY26 guide $31.1-31.3bn and $2.40-2.60, 39-week actuals of $23,510mm and $1.95, so implied Q4 sales of $7.59-7.79bn and implied Q4 EPS of $0.45-0.65, with the $0.62 consensus at the 85th percentile. That is the problem. This is a calculation performed on two published numbers -- the company's own narrowed guidance from 2026-06-09 and a consensus print that is, by construction, the price. It requires no non-public input and it is the first calculation any sell-side preview runs. It is also less sharp than it looks. A $0.20-wide implied band around a $0.62 estimate is plus or minus 16%, so 'the 85th percentile' is spurious precision on a quarter where a single item -- fuel recovery, a further insurance recovery, a productivity pull-forward -- swings more than the whole band, and narrowed Q4 ranges are routinely exceeded. And the market has already been taught this lesson the hard way: on 2026-06-09 UNFI missed revenue by roughly $236mm against a $7.96bn consensus, missed EPS $0.77 versus $0.79, merely narrowed rather than raised the guide, and lost 10.28%. Across FY26 the company cut sales guidance from $31.6-32.0bn while raising adjusted EPS from $1.50-2.30 to $2.40-2.60 -- so 'revenue estimates at the guide floor, EPS estimates near the guide top' is not an asymmetry the hunter found, it is the exact residue of a year in which sales guidance came down twice and EPS guidance went up twice, and it is what the -20.9%-from-high, -6.6%-over-20-days tape reflects.

findings.finding: The first FY27 guide has to be set against a fuel base far above FY26's with only partial hedging, and UNFI's own multi-year frame gives it cover to guide flat: EIA weekly diesel was $5.599/gal on 2026-08-31 versus $3.708 a year earlier (+51%), the fiscal-Q1-to-date August average is $5.46 versus $3.74 (+46%), and against FY24 adjusted EBITDA of $518m the published "low-double-digit average annual Adjusted EBITDA growth from FY24 to FY27" target is satisfied by FY27 of roughly $690-730m - i.e. flat to +5% on the FY26 guide midpoint of $695m - even though the longer-term algorithm management talks to is high-single-digit EBITDA growth.
findings.adversary_note: The diesel data is exactly right and I verified it against the EIA series itself: $5.599/gal on 2026-08-31 against $3.651 on 2025-08-26, with August 2026 weeks of $5.348, $5.257, $5.454, $5.652, $5.599 versus roughly $3.70 a year earlier. But the target arithmetic that carries the conclusion is factually wrong. The published target is 'Low-double digit average annual growth, ~$800 million target for fiscal 2028' -- the terminal year is FY2028, not FY2027, and there is no published 'FY24 to FY27' EBITDA target to be satisfied. Run it correctly: from the FY24 base of $518mm to ~$800mm in FY28 is about 11.5% a year, whose FY27 waypoint is ~$717mm; and the smooth path from the $695mm FY26 midpoint to $800mm in FY28 is +7.3% a year, i.e. FY27 of about $745mm. So the correct frame gives management cover to guide FY27 in the +3% to +7% range, not flat. Flat at $695mm would require FY28 to jump 15% to hit the published $800mm and would visibly break management's own bridge -- and it would contradict what they told the market on 2026-06-09, which is that FY27 returns to low-single-digit sales growth with improving profitability. The hunter's $690-730mm band happens to brush the bottom of the correct path, so the numerical conclusion is not void, but the 'cover to guide flat' reading is a misreading of the target table. On the priced side: diesel at record August highs is front-page macro, covered by Transport Topics, FleetOwner and Qz through August, published sell-side commentary already names 'fuel costs and transportation expense' as the specific FY27 uncertainty for UNFI, and the tape has been marking it -- $47.90 on 2026-08-13 to $43.94 on 2026-09-04. What I concede is magnitude: fuel up ~46% on a $31bn distributor's transportation base is tens of millions against a $695mm EBITDA even after partial recovery, and that scale is not drawn out anywhere I can find.

findings.finding: The executive who will deliver UNFI's first FY27 guidance started five weeks ago: the 2026-07-09 8-K appointed Alfredo Luchini CFO effective 2026-08-10 (from Carrier Climate Solutions Americas), moved Matteo Tarditi from President/CFO to President/COO, elevated Louis Martin to Chief Commercial Officer and disclosed Mark Bushway's exit - and a fifth change, Matt Echols ceasing to be Chief Corporate Affairs Officer effective 2026-08-24, was disclosed only in a Form 4 remark filed 2026-08-27, with no Item 5.02 8-K, no press release and no trade-press coverage.
findings.adversary_note: This is the same claim as UNFI-h1#1 and it is anchored more explicitly on the one document that makes it priced. The 8-K it cites (report date 2026-07-07, filed 2026-07-09) came with exhibit 99.1, a leadership-announcement press release, distributed via Businesswire on 2026-07-09 and picked up within two days by TipRanks, The Shelby Report, Supermarket News, Progressive Grocer, Mass Market Retailers, Abasto and Distribution Strategy Group -- all four of the changes the finding lists (Luchini CFO effective 2026-08-10 from Carrier Climate Solutions Americas, Tarditi to President/COO, Martin to Chief Commercial Officer, Bushway's exit) were in the wire copy. The finding's own framing concedes this: it says four of the five were 8-K'd and press-released. The fifth, Echols, I verified is genuinely unpublished outside the Form 4 remark -- I searched and found only his 2022 appointment coverage and the July reorganisation stories, none of which mention a departure. But Chief Corporate Affairs Officer is a communications and public-affairs seat with no P&L, no guidance role and no analyst relationship; treating it as the fact that reprices a name with a 12.02% implied move is a category error. And 'the executive who will deliver the first FY27 guide started five weeks ago' has been knowable, to the day, since 2026-07-09.

findings.finding: Waterdrop's Q1 2026 net profit FELL 8.9% year over year to RMB98.4m from RMB108.2m, and operating profit rose only 5.4% (RMB80.0m vs RMB75.9m) on revenue up 64.8%, because sales and marketing expense tripled — up 213.8% to RMB541.1m from RMB172.4m, or 43.6% of revenue — so the entire 'AI-driven growth' story is currently producing no incremental profit, and the Q2 2026 comparative is Q2 2025's RMB140.2m, 42% above the Q1 2026 run-rate.
findings.adversary_note: Every number in this claim is correct, and every one of them is already public in the form the claim uses. The Q1 2026 release (SEC 6-K exhibit, dated June 16/filed June 17 2026) states net profit RMB98.4m vs RMB108.2m, operating profit RMB80.0m vs RMB75.9m (+5.3%), revenue RMB1,242.2m (+64.8%) and S&M RMB541.1m (+213.8%) verbatim. The market traded that release on 2026-06-17 and moved +2.34%. More damaging: on the same day's call management GUIDED to exactly the claim's thesis -- 'approximately 40% top-line growth for 2026, with operating profit scale expected to remain broadly stable' as marketing investment rises -- and that sentence was carried in at least five transcripts (Motley Fool, Benzinga, Globe and Mail, AOL, MarketBeat). 'Growth is producing no incremental profit' is not a discovery; it is the company's own stated 2026 plan, which puts this in the 90-100 'restates published guidance' band. The one element I could not find published is the explicit Q2-comp arithmetic (Q2 2025's RMB140.2m sits 42% above the Q1 2026 run-rate), and that is the only reason this is not 95. But the sizing on that piece is also weaker than it looks, because it ignores seasonality: 2025's quarterly net profit ran 108.2 / 140.2 / 158.4 / 162.1, so Q1->Q2 rose 29.6% seasonally in 2025 too. Apply the same seasonal step to Q1 2026's 98.4m and Q2 2026 lands near RMB128m, i.e. roughly -9% YoY -- the same YoY delta Q1 already printed, not a new deterioration. The market has now seen two consecutive prints of this exact pattern (Q4 2025 on 2026-03-25: revenue +105.5%, S&M +178.4%, operating profit RMB83.9m against a Q1-Q3 2025 average of ~RMB96m; move -1.20%) and priced each inside 2.5%.

findings.finding: Waterdrop's current US$50m share repurchase authorisation runs 'during the 12-month period through September 9, 2026' — expiring the day AFTER this 2026-09-08 print — and it has been almost unused: cumulative repurchases went from approximately US$109.0m (55.7m ADSs) at 2025-08-31 to approximately US$120.1m (61.8m ADSs) at 2026-05-31, so roughly US$11m of the US$50m was spent in nine months; the company has launched a new programme every September for five straight years (2021, 2022, 2023, 2024, 2025) and announced the 2025 one inside the Q2 earnings release itself, and its semi-annual dividend's second-half tranche has likewise been declared with the September release (ex-dates 2024-10-11 and 2025-10-10), where US$0.03 per ADS is now 2.86% of a US$1.0495 spot versus roughly 1.5% a year ago.
findings.adversary_note: The facts check out exactly and I concede all of them. The 2025-09-04 release says verbatim 'up to US$50 million during the 12-month period through September 9, 2026' and gives cumulative repurchases of ~US$109.0m / 55.7m ADSs at 2025-08-31; the Q1 2026 release gives ~US$120.1m / 61.8m ADSs at 2026-05-31, so ~US$11m of US$50m in nine months. The September ritual is real: I confirmed the same US$50m/12-month authorisation in the Q2 2023 release (through 2023-09-06) and the Q2 2024 release (through 2025-09-09), and the dividend tranches at record dates 2024-10-11 (US$0.02) and 2025-10-10 (US$0.03). US$0.03 / 1.0495 = 2.86% is arithmetically right. What I dispute is the sizing, on three grounds. First, the authorisation expiry is not obscure -- it is in a PR Newswire release syndicated to Nasdaq, Yahoo Finance, Barchart, Manila Times and Macau Business, and a five-consecutive-year renewal pattern is the textbook 'structural and known' case: the renewal is the base case, so only a NON-renewal is information. Second, the 'barely used' number is closer to public than the claim implies -- Simply Wall St published 'repurchased 5,278,431 shares for approximately US$9.54 million by May 31, 2026' on 2026-08-07, three weeks before this print, in the same article discussing capital allocation. Third and most decisive, the exact event being forecast has already been run: on 2025-09-04 Waterdrop announced, in one release, a fresh US$50m authorisation AND a dividend that was up 50% on the prior one, and the stock moved +2.25%. A repeat with the same nominal US$0.03 and the same US$50m cannot reasonably be worth more than that, and a renewal of an authorisation that went ~78% unused is close to a non-event -- what moves the stock is buying, and the published run-rate is ~US$1.2m/month against ~US$192k/day of dollar volume. The higher percentage yield is not new information; it is the observable consequence of a price anyone can see on their screen.

findings.finding: China's eight financial and internet regulators jointly issued the Administrative Measures for Online Marketing of Financial Products on 2026-04-24, effective 2026-09-30 — 22 days after this print — whose Article 20 bars third-party internet platforms (defined as sites and apps 'not self-operated by a financial institution') from intervening or covertly intervening in sales-contract signing, fund transfer or suitability assessment, and from conducting interactive consultation with consumers about financial products, which puts a hard compliance date on the traffic architecture behind Waterdrop's insurance marketplace and its non-licensed Waterdrop Medical Crowdfunding funnel.
findings.adversary_note: The regulation is real and the dates are right -- gov.cn and Xinhua both carry it as issued 2026-04-24 by eight departments, effective 2026-09-30 -- but it was not published obscurely and it does not reach the numbers in this print. Caixin Global ran 'China Imposes Sweeping Curbs on Online Financial Marketing' in English on 2026-04-28; Xinhua, chinanews, Bastille Post, Cointelegraph and Digital Watch all covered it, and at least four major PRC firms (King & Wood Mallesons, Zhong Lun, Haiwen, Guantao) published client analyses specifically flagging the impact on 'lead-generation and traffic-direction business models'. That is mainstream, sector-connected publication four months before the print. The stock has already taken the derating: WDH sits 47.3% below its 52-week high and only 7.9% above its low, and a 2026-08-08 Seeking Alpha piece describes it as having 'lost close to half its market cap in 2026' with 'headwinds... for more than one reason' and fair value cut from $2.32 to $1.94. Two further precision points. Article 20's first limb is conditional, not absolute: the Chinese text reads '不得违反法律法规、国家金融管理规定介入或变相介入' -- platforms may not intervene *in contravention of* laws and financial-administration rules -- so the claim's rendering as a flat bar overstates it; only the second limb ('不得就金融产品与消费者和投资者进行互动咨询') is unconditional. And the definitional hook may not catch Waterdrop's core business at all: its insurance operation runs through Shuidi (formerly Baoduoduo) Insurance Brokerage Co., a licensed PRC insurance broker, which makes it a licensed financial institution for these purposes rather than a 'third-party internet platform not self-operated by a financial institution'. Finally, the mechanism does not reach the Q2 numbers -- the quarter ended 2026-06-30, three months before effectiveness -- and management did not mention the rules on the 2026-06-17 call despite them having been public for eight weeks, and no analyst asked. It can only enter the print through commentary or a guidance haircut.

findings.finding: Waterdrop turned over both of its finance-oversight seats in the five weeks immediately before this print: independent director Heping Feng left the board effective 2026-07-01 and was replaced by Qianfei Chang as independent director and audit committee chair (6-K, 2026-06-23), and then the vice president of finance and head of finance, Xiaoying Xu, resigned effective 2026-07-31 (6-K, 2026-07-24).
findings.adversary_note: Both filings are real, both dates are right, and both have already had their day in the market. The 2026-06-23 6-K exhibit confirms Heping Feng's departure effective 2026-07-01 and Qianfei Chang's same-day appointment as independent director and audit committee chair; the 2026-07-24 6-K confirms Xiaoying Xu's resignation as vice president of finance and head of finance effective 2026-07-31. But the framing of 'turned over both finance-oversight seats' does most of the work and the documents do not support it. The audit committee was never vacant: Chang took the chair the same day Feng left, and she is a China CPA with an MBA in finance and 15+ years of financial-management and audit-oversight experience -- on the face of the filing an upgrade for the seat, not a hole in it. Xu's exit is stated as 'personal reasons' with the explicit 'not due to any dispute or disagreement with the Company' language, and Waterdrop has no CFO role for her to have been -- there is nothing here forcing a restatement, an auditor change or a controls disclosure, none of which is alleged. Both events are on the wire, not just on EDGAR: TipRanks ran 'Waterdrop Announces Finance Chief Resignation Effective July 31, 2026', StockTitan carried the 6-K, Investing.com covered the board changes, and Simply Wall St / Yahoo Finance published a dedicated analytical piece on 2026-08-07 asking precisely the hunter's question -- 'What Does Waterdrop's (WDH) Finance Chief Exit Reveal About Its AI Investment And Capital Return Plans?'. That is the claim's own inference, already written up. Decisively, the baseline records what the market did on each date: -0.83% on 2026-06-23 and +2.68% on 2026-07-24, both consistent with noise on a 183k-share name, and the stock is +5.7% over the five days into the print. Timing also cuts against it: Xu was in post for the whole of the quarter being reported, which closed 2026-06-30, a month before she left.

findings.finding: The US airline earnings cycle broke inside ABM's fiscal Q3 (1 May - 31 July 2026) and after ABM last guided: American cut FY26 guidance to a -$0.65 to +$0.65 range and guided Q3 to an adjusted loss of $0.10-$0.70, Southwest cut FY26 EPS to $3.25-$4.25 and trimmed capacity growth to ~1.5%, and Alaska suspended guidance and cut May and June capacity, on jet fuel of $3.65-$4.50/gal — while ABM's Aviation segment operating margin had already collapsed to 5.25% in Q2 FY26 ($16.3M profit on $310.8M revenue) from 6.34% a year earlier, and ABM runs 1,000+ conventionally fuelled shuttle buses and 2,000+ parking locations on largely fixed-price contracts.
findings.adversary_note: Every constituent fact here is wire copy, and the two ABM-side facts are ABM's own published words with a stated cause that is not airline distress. The airline cuts: American's first 2026 guidance cut was 2026-04-23 and Alaska's suspension was April 2026 -- both BEFORE ABM guided on 2026-06-05, so the claim's framing ('after ABM last guided') is factually wrong for two of its three carriers. The claim's own source also reports Delta affirming $6.50-7.50 and United RAISING to $9-11, so the sector bifurcated rather than broke, and Delta/United are the carriers most relevant to major-hub turn volume. American's six route suspensions were announced 2026-06-04 and run 2026-08-05 to 2026-10-05 -- entirely outside ABM's fiscal Q3, which ended 31 July; they land in Q4. On the ABM side, the 5.25% Aviation margin is arithmetically correct ($16.3M/$310.8M) but was disclosed by ABM itself on 2026-06-05 and attributed by management to 'weather-related and ramp-up cost inefficiencies' (the London Heathrow ramp), alongside 20% Aviation revenue growth on 'healthy domestic air travel trends' -- and the stock rose 6.67% that day with all of it on the table. The bridge is the weak part: ABM bills per turn, per cabin, per parking transaction and per shuttle hour against traffic and airport/airline contracts, not against airline EPS; a fuel-driven EPS collapse at a carrier whose revenue is still growing does not reduce ABM's billable units inside a 92-day window. The one channel that genuinely lands in 1 May - 31 July is ABM's own diesel/gasoline bill on its bus fleet, and ABM's own marketing puts that fleet at '800+ buses' rather than 1,000+; on plausible utilisation a $1/gal move is order $2M pre-tax a quarter, roughly $0.02-0.03 of EPS against a $0.97 consensus -- under 1% of the quarter and an order of magnitude inside the 3.33% deadband. Verdict: I concede the facts about the airlines and about ABM's Q2 margin, and reject the bridge -- this is true about the source companies and close to worthless about ABM's Q3 P&L.

findings.finding: The two closest public reads on the segment ABM said would drive its back-half step-up printed records for the April-June 2026 window after ABM last spoke: Comfort Systems reported revenue +50% to $3.27bn, diluted EPS $12.53 vs $6.53, and backlog of $14.06bn at 30 June 2026 against $8.12bn a year earlier, and EMCOR raised FY26 revenue guidance to $20.0-20.5bn from $18.5-19.25bn and EPS to $32.00-33.25 from $28.25-29.75 — corroborating the 'meaningful ramp' in Technical Solutions and M&D volume ABM guided to on 2026-06-05, in a stock that has not participated at all.
findings.adversary_note: The FIX and EMCOR facts check out exactly as stated -- FIX revenue $3.27bn (+50%), EPS $12.53 vs $6.53, backlog $14.06bn at 30 June vs $8.12bn; EMCOR to $20.0-20.5bn from $18.5-19.25bn and $32.00-33.25 from $28.25-29.75 -- but both are the loudest wire-copy events of the July reporting season, EMCOR traded up 7.1% on its raise, and the AI/data-centre capex cycle is the single most-told story in this market. Two things break the claim as stated. First, the premise 'in a stock that has not participated at all' is false on the tape: ABM was $49.36 on 2026-07-30, up 23.7% over the prior 90 days, and set its 52-week high at $50.12 in that same window -- spot 47.02 is 4.7% below it and 25.8% above the low. ABM participated; it has since given back ~5%, which is a different and much smaller claim. Second, the ramp is not just published, it is in the consensus number: ABM guided the back half on 2026-06-05 to 'meaningfully higher volume in ATS and M&D' with improved mix, explicitly citing 'battery energy storage systems and datacenter-related services' behind ATS's 27% growth, reaffirmed FY26 at $3.85-4.15, and the sell side now carries Q3 FY26 at $0.97 against $0.82 actual a year ago -- an 18% step-up already required of the print. The bridge is also thinner than the size of the FIX/EME numbers suggests: FIX and EME are pure-play hyperscale MEP construction; ABM's Technical Solutions is $267.3M of revenue at a 6.3% operating margin, about 11-12% of ABM, doing retrofit, microgrid, BESS, EV charging and mission-critical facility services. A +50% quarter at FIX says the cycle is alive; it says nothing about ABM's own project timing, which is precisely the variable that produced -9.07% on 2025-06-06 and -8.67% on 2025-03-12. Even a strong ATS quarter -- say 35% growth with 100bp of mix -- is order $5-8M of incremental operating profit, roughly $0.06-0.10 of EPS, and much of that is the guided path rather than a surprise. What keeps this off 90 is one genuinely under-drawn item: nobody has modelled an inflection in ABM's own ATS backlog disclosure on the scale of FIX's +73% or EMCOR's +44% RPO, and that number does land in this print.

findings.finding: The 'digital asset treasury' behind the 2026-08-04 buyback announcement is majority-encumbered: at 2026-03-31 Canaan owned only 802.6 bitcoins outright (plus 63.4 held as customer deposits), while 905.0 bitcoins were pledged for secured term loans and 100.0 more were transferred into a fixed-term product, against US$54.5m of loans (US$21.14m current + US$33.37m long-term).
findings.adversary_note: Every number in this claim is verbatim from the 19-May Q1 exhibit, which I fetched and confirmed (802.6 owned + 63.4 customer deposits in digital assets; 905.0 pledged + 100.0 fixed-term in cryptocurrency receivable; loans US$21,140k current + US$33,373k long-term). The fact is correct and the arithmetic checks (1,005 of 1,871 = 53.7% encumbered). But the encumbrance was published in trade press in direct connection with the buyback two days after the announcement: CryptoSlate on 2026-08-06 wrote 'It had also pledged 905 BTC for secured term loans and placed another 100 BTC in a fixed-term product' under the headline 'Canaan can use crypto to buy back nearly 20% of its market value while its core business burns cash' - i.e. the exact 'headline treasury is not free' thesis, in print, with the pledge figure. Two further weaknesses on sizing. First, applying a 2026-03-31 encumbrance split to the 2026-07-31 treasury of 1,917 BTC is an extrapolation the company has not confirmed. Second, and worse for the sign: BTC has gone from $58,504 on 2026-06-30 to $77,934 on 2026-09-03, so US$54.5m of secured loans is now collateralised by ~1,005 BTC worth ~$78m rather than ~$59m - the coverage on the pledge has improved materially since the balance-sheet date, which makes the encumbrance less binding now than when it was published, not more.

findings.finding: Canaan's funded forward order book has not been rebuilt: contract liabilities (customer advances) were US$7.739m at 2026-03-31 and US$9.317m at 2025-12-31, against 'nearly $87 million' at 2025-09-30 when over 85% came from North American clients - and no new Avalon purchase-order press release has appeared at any point between June and September 2026.
findings.adversary_note: Both anchors are real and both are public: $7,739k contract liabilities at 2026-03-31 against $9,317k at 2025-12-31 is a line in the 19-May exhibit I fetched, and the 'nearly $87 million ... over 85% from North American clients' comes from the Q3 2025 earnings call, whose transcript is free on Motley Fool. The juxtaposition - a 91% collapse in the funded order book - I could not find drawn out anywhere, and that is the strongest thing about this finding. What kills most of its value is that the implication has already been stated by the company in stronger form and priced: Canaan guided Q2 revenue to $35-45m on 2026-05-19 and the stock fell 13.66% that day. A collapsed order book and a $35-45m guide are the same statement about near-term revenue, and the company's version is the one the market traded on. The 'no new Avalon purchase-order press release between June and September 2026' leg is the weakest part - absence of a discretionary press release is not a disclosure, PO announcements are opportunistic (the Cipher A1566 release was 2024), and the 19-May release did in fact announce a Nordic district-heating win with a 6 MW follow-on order placed in March 2026, so the company was still announcing demand as of the last print. The genuinely unpriced datum is the 2026-06-30 contract-liabilities balance, which arrives at this print, but that is new information arriving rather than a finding about it.

findings.finding: Q2 exit-rate was artificially crushed and has already fully recovered: non-JV month-end operating hashrate was 3.36 EH/s against 10.05 EH/s installed at 2026-06-30 (grid maintenance, on top of a 'planned expiration of a hosting agreement' in May that cut non-JV installed capacity from 266.3 MW in April to 246.2 MW), and by 2026-07-31 non-JV operating was back to 10.05 EH/s - equal to installed - with the average revenue split improving from 60.3% to 60.6%.
findings.adversary_note: The facts are right but they are in company press releases carried by PR Newswire, Morningstar and StockTitan on the day, and I verified both halves from the filings. The 2026-07-14 6-K exhibit gives June non-JV operating hashrate 3.36 EH/s against installed 10.05 EH/s, 246.2 MW installed capacity, 60.3% average revenue split, and names 'grid maintenance at one of our facilities'. The recovery leg is not in that document - the July update, filed as a 6-K on 2026-08-17, is where operating returns to 10.05 EH/s equal to installed, with 46 BTC mined. So the brief's citation is wrong on the recovery: a 2026-07-14 filing cannot report 2026-07-31 data. The fact survives the citation error, but that is exactly the problem for the finding: monthly operational disclosure is the mechanism that stops a weak Q2 mining line being a surprise. The market has had the June exit rate since 2026-07-14 and the July recovery since 2026-08-17, and the baseline shows +0.69% and -0.43% on those dates - no reaction, because there was nothing to react to. This is the only mitigating claim of the eight and I concede it points the right way, but a self-mining segment that produced $19.1m of a $62.7m Q1 cannot carry much of a $0.36 stock's print when its inputs are already published monthly.

findings.finding: Inventory of US$139.1m at 2026-03-31 sits against a Q2 revenue guide of US$35-45m and a Q1 gross LOSS of US$22.9m on US$62.7m of revenue, while the current-generation Avalon A16 (12.8 J/TH, launched October 2025) leaves the A15-era stock as the write-down candidate - Canaan's own self-mining fleet is still running at 23.7 J/TH global and 17.9 J/TH in North America.
findings.adversary_note: I verified inventory of $139,078k at 2026-03-31 (down from $180,816k), the $22.9m Q1 gross loss and the $35-45m Q2 guide, all in the 19-May exhibit. But the write-down inference is not an inference the market has to make - it has already been made, twice, in public. Press and vendor coverage of the Q1 print stated that the $23m gross loss was 'driven by a $25M non-cash inventory write-down', so the market has seen this exact charge one quarter ago and repriced for it (-13.66%). More damaging: on the Q1 call management said out loud that for older-generation machines 'the company still had some inventory and lowered the price to try to clear that inventory within quarter two' - i.e. management pre-announced a Q2 margin hit on A15-era stock on 2026-05-19. A second write-down is therefore the single most telegraphed item in this print, and it is non-cash, on a stock whose 20-day realised vol is 183% and whose marginal buyer over the last month has been crypto-beta flow following the CLARITY Act rally, not a gross-margin analyst. The self-mining efficiency figures (23.7 J/TH global, 17.9 J/TH North America) are published monthly and are about the mining fleet, not the saleable inventory, so they do not add to the write-down case.

findings.finding: Sell-side numbers for CAN were never marked down to Canaan's own guidance: the terminal Q2 revenue consensus is $53.87-55.41m against the company's 19-May guide of $35-45m, and FY2026 consensus of $269.23m (6 analysts, S&P Global, as of 2026-07-24) requires H2 revenue ~65% above an H1 that will total roughly $98-108m — so both the Q2 headline and any Q3 guide mechanically print as a large 'miss', and investing.com's feed has already auto-published a Q2 revenue 'actual' of $31.20m vs $55.41m consensus (below the low end of guidance) in an article timestamped 2026-09-03 06:27.
findings.adversary_note: The investing.com leg is not evidence and should be struck. I fetched the page: it lists the 2026-09-08 event under period label 'Q3 2026 (09/2026)' - the wrong quarter, since the release covers the quarter ended 2026-06-30 - with EPS 'actual' -$0.063 and revenue 'actual' $31.20M for an event that has not occurred. That is an auto-populated placeholder. The same column is demonstrably broken for this issuer on real quarters: it carries Q1 2026 EPS 'actual' of -$0.86 against a company-reported GAAP loss of $0.13 per ADS and a net loss of $88.7m on 744.84m ADS (~$0.12/ADS), so the vendor's EPS series is off by roughly 7x and mixes bases. Worse for the claim, if investing.com's $55.41m forecast is genuinely tagged to the 09/2026 quarter, then comparing it to Q2 guidance of $35-45m is apples-to-oranges and the whole 'never marked down' gap may be a labelling artifact. Does the claim survive without that page? Partly, yes, and I concede that: stockanalysis.com independently shows FY2026 revenue consensus of $269.23m from 4 analysts last updated 2026-07-24, and Simply Wall St / Quartr independently show a next-quarter revenue consensus of $53.87m. So consensus above guidance is corroborated. But it is corroborated on free, public, retail-facing pages - which puts it in the published-and-visible band, not the obscure band - and there is a strong counter-example inside the same data: for Q1 the vendor consensus was $64.68m against actual $62.7m 'in line with guidance', i.e. analysts on this name DO mark to guidance, which suggests the $53-55m figure is a stale or mis-tagged aggregate rather than a live view. Finally, the FY arithmetic is less damning than stated: FY $269m against an H1 of ~$103m implies H2 of ~$166m, versus a $196.3m Q4 2025 alone - not an obviously impossible H2 for a rig vendor with BTC back at $77.9k after a +24% August. Sell-side consensus from 4-6 analysts is also not the price-setter on a $261m FPI trading 22m shares a day.

findings.finding: The liquidity line is the print's real unknown: cash fell from $80.8m at 2025-12-31 to $43.5m at 2026-03-31 (a $37.3m burn in one quarter) against $106.4m of current liabilities and $21.1m of loans due inside a year, 905 of 1,871 bitcoins were pledged as collateral for $54.5m of secured term loans, and Q2 revenue was guided 30-45% lower than Q1 — so the 30-June balance sheet, struck with BTC at $58,504 on 2026-06-30 (BTC's worst quarter in years, -34% YTD), is where the market first sees how little unencumbered liquidity is left behind the '$130m treasury' headline.
findings.adversary_note: Every 2026-03-31 component here is correct - I confirmed cash $43,451k against $80,778k, loans $21,140k current, 905 BTC pledged against $54.5m of secured term loans - and the BTC print of $58,504 at 2026-06-30 is exact ($58,503.73 per Fortune). But this is the same document and, crucially, the same published aggregation as CAN-h1#0: CryptoSlate on 2026-08-06 put the cash-versus-current-liabilities comparison in print in the same terms the finding uses - '$43.5 million in cash against $106.4 million in current liabilities at March 31' - alongside the 905 pledged BTC and the distinction between headline treasury value and assets ready for use. So the framing is not new. Two things cut the sign. First, the 19-May release also disclosed approximately US$42 million of customer cash collections in April 2026, which the finding omits and which offsets a large share of the $37.3m Q1 burn - the market has had that offset for four months. Second, a 2026-06-30 balance sheet struck at BTC $58,504 is a stale mark: BTC is $77,934 as of 2026-09-03, so the market prices today's ~$159m treasury, not June's ~$119m one, and a weak 6/30 liquidity snapshot is straightforwardly discountable as a low-water mark. Against that, management authorised a $30m crypto-funded buyback on 2026-08-04 and, per stockanalysis.com's news list, management members bought ADS in the open market - both are revealed-preference statements that insiders do not think liquidity is at the wall. What genuinely is unpriced is the 6/30 unencumbered-cash number itself, but 'a new balance sheet arrives at the print' is a description of earnings, not a finding.

findings.finding: The stated trigger for the crypto-funded buyback has been extinguished by the rally it helped cause: on 2026-08-04 Canaan justified monetising digital assets by saying it was 'trading below the combined value of its digital assets holdings and its cash and cash equivalents as reported on March 31, 2026' ($130m treasury as of 3 August plus $43.5m cash = $173.5m, against a $144.7m market cap on 6 August), but after a 108.8% August the market cap is $261.0m while the treasury of 1,917 BTC and 3,952 ETH is worth roughly $165m at BTC ~$81.0k and ETH ~$2.4-2.5k — so on the company's own yardstick the stock now trades at roughly a 25% premium rather than a 17% discount, and the repurchase authorisation expires 2026-12-12.
findings.adversary_note: The arithmetic is sound and if anything conservative - I checked it independently. Market cap is $260.70m at $0.35 on 744.84m shares (stockanalysis.com, 2026-09-04 10:52 EDT). Treasury of 1,917 BTC at $77,934 (2026-09-03) is $149.4m, plus 3,952 ETH at ~$2,391-2,495 is ~$9.5-9.9m, so ~$159m - not $165m, because BTC is $77.9k rather than the $81.0k assumed. On the company's own 3-August yardstick that is $159m + $43.5m cash = ~$202.6m against $260.7m, a premium of ~29%, so the claim understates its own case. The problem is that this is the most mechanically visible number in the entire crypto-equity complex: mNAV is computed from two public prices and a public share count, The Block maintains a live CAN treasury page, and the crossover was already written up - ts2.tech published 'Trump Crypto Push Lifts Canaan Stock (CAN) 13% as Treasury Covers 72% of Market Value' in late August, with treasury at $146.1m against a market cap implying ~$202m, i.e. the discount was already reported as gone. On sign, the claim is also contestable: nothing in the 2026-08-04 authorisation conditions the buyback on a discount, the programme runs to 2026-12-12 regardless, monetising crypto at $77.9k buys back more shares per BTC than at $58.5k, and management were buying ADS in the open market. 'The stated rationale no longer holds' is a rhetorical point about a press release, not a cash-flow change.

findings.finding: The Nasdaq minimum-bid arithmetic is now impossible without a capital-structure action: the ADS must close at or above $1.00 for 10 consecutive business days by 2027-01-11, which from $0.3501 is +186%, so an ADS ratio change (currently 1 ADS = 15 Class A ordinary shares) has to be noticed to holders around November to be effective in time — and the 8 September call is the first scheduled management appearance since the deadline was granted.
findings.adversary_note: The facts check out against the filing: I confirmed the 2027-01-11 deadline after a 180-day extension, the $1.00-for-ten-consecutive-business-days test, and 1 ADS = 15 Class A ordinary shares; +186% from $0.3501 is correct arithmetic. It is also true that the 8 September call is the first scheduled management appearance since 2026-07-15, since the monthly production updates are press releases with no call. But the whole situation is published and was covered on the day by Yahoo Finance and Blockspace, and the company's own release says it 'intends to continue monitoring the closing bid price ... and will evaluate all available options during the second compliance period' - so the need for a capital-structure action is stated by the issuer, in public, and the market's response was +0.69%. This is the textbook case of structural-and-known: a sub-$1 Nasdaq name with an ADS-ratio lever and a stated deadline is about as far from novel as a finding gets, and age is not novelty. The November notice timing is the hunter's own inference and not published, which is the finding's one real contribution, but it also argues against reaching this print - nothing obliges management to announce a ratio change on 8 September, the deadline is four months out, and the 2027-01-11 date sits two quarters beyond this window. On top of that, an ADS-ratio change is value-neutral by construction, and the +113.76% move off the 52-week low shows a tape on which a further +186% over four months is not the arithmetic impossibility the claim asserts.

findings.finding: On 2026-08-12 Gamehaus said it will 'progressively optimize its third-party publishing business in casual titles, and in particular in the social casino category' and manage the existing portfolio 'on a cash flow- and profitability-oriented basis, with user acquisition and operating expenditure allocated according to return on investment rather than scale of installed base' - and that 'This approach took effect during the current quarter', i.e. the July-September quarter now in progress, which is exactly the quarter for which the 2026-09-08 release will issue its forward revenue guide.
findings.adversary_note: The quoted language is not obscure — it is verbatim from a PRNewswire release of 2026-08-12 that was syndicated to AOL, TradingView, MarketBeat and StockTitan the same morning, and the sentence the hunter leans on ('This approach took effect during the current quarter') is in the release itself, not derived. The mechanism is real and I concede it reaches this print: Gamehaus guides the forward quarter in every results release (FY25 print of 2025-09-09 guided Q1 FY26 to $27-30m; Q3 FY26 print of 2026-06-08 guided Q4 FY26 to $23-26m), so a Q1 FY27 guide on 2026-09-08 is close to certain. What is *not* new is the underlying story: 'revenue down because we deliberately cut user acquisition' has been the company's own published explanation since the FY25 release of 2025-09-09 ('strategic reduction in user acquisition spending and the Company's deliberate adjustment to its marketing approach'), and revenue has printed -18.7% FY25, -7.5% Q1 FY26, -9.1% Q3 FY26 with a Q4 guide below Q4 FY25's $30.7m. A weaker forward guide is the trend, not a surprise. Two things hold my number below 70 rather than at 85. First, the most widely syndicated third-party interpretation of the 08-12 release was *positive* — StockTitan's Rhea-AI tag was 'Positive / Moderate', framing the pivot as higher-margin, and explicitly noted 'no financial guidance or quantified impact provided'. Nobody anywhere has drawn the line from that paragraph to a specific Q1 FY27 revenue guide cut. Second, I decline to lean on the price reaction as evidence of pricing: GMHS fell -5.99% on 2026-08-12 and -5.19% on 2026-08-13, which is directionally consistent, but on 22,908 and 6,192 shares — about $22k of total turnover. An 11% two-session decline on $22k of trade is one seller, not a market absorbing an announcement, and on this book 'the market has priced it' is not establishable either way. So: the fact is wire copy, the sizing is nowhere, and I score the composite at 55 rather than splitting the difference silently.

findings.finding: Three separate structural events sit unabsorbed in front of the print: a $200,000,000 mixed-securities F-3 shelf filed 2026-07-28 and declared effective 2026-08-12 (about 4.5x the ~$44m market cap, with no prospectus supplement drawn as of 2026-09-04), a Nasdaq minimum-bid-price deficiency letter dated 2026-07-10 with a 2027-01-06 compliance deadline and no committed remedy, and a 2026-07-10 extraordinary general meeting that raised Class B voting power from 15 to 50 votes per share - control-proofing the founder immediately before an effective shelf.
findings.adversary_note: All three legs are published, two of them prominently, and the headline sizing is contradicted by the cover page of the document the hunter cites. (1) The Nasdaq minimum-bid deficiency got its own PRNewswire release on 2026-07-13 06:00 ET plus MarketScreener pickup, and the tape printed -2.38% that session — this is the single most wire-covered fact in the brief and it is one of the baseline's own 'reaction' rows. (2) The F-3 was covered by StockTitan on filing. (3) The Class B 15-to-50 vote increase was in an EGM proxy filed to EDGAR on 2026-06-24, approved 2026-07-10, results filed 2026-07-14 (+1.33% that session), and is restated on the F-3 cover; the stock rose +9.84% on the day the proxy proposing it was filed, so there is no unabsorbed negative reaction to point at. The 'unabsorbed' framing is therefore wrong for the two material legs. More importantly, the sizing is factually wrong, not merely contested. '$200,000,000 ... about 4.5x the ~$44m market cap' is the registered ceiling, but the F-3 cover states non-affiliate float of 27,038,542 Class A shares worth US$23,523,531.54 at $0.87 and expressly notes the Form F-3 General Instruction I.B.5/I.B.6 limitation capping primary sales at one-third of that float in any 12 months — roughly US$7.8m, about 17% of market cap, not 450%. The dilution capacity the hunter sized is overstated by about 25x, and the correction is on page one of the URL given as the source. Two further points: the Nasdaq clock runs to 2027-01-06 and the standard remedy is a reverse split, neither of which is an earnings-release event; and Class B was already held by a single holder (Chairman Feng Xie) at 15 votes per share, so 15-to-50 raises a control margin he almost certainly already had — the marginal governance effect is small. Nothing in this leg resolves on 2026-09-08.

findings.finding: The $5m buyback that caused a +105% single-day move when announced on 2025-08-28/30 was 88% unused when it expired: the 2026-08-28 6-K discloses only about 518,063 Class A shares repurchased for roughly $600,000 (an average near $1.16), meaning the company stopped buying entirely as the stock fell from ~$1.16 to a 52-week low near $0.67, and then extended the same authorisation unchanged to 2027-08-28.
findings.adversary_note: The headline fact is wire copy from three months ago and one of the sub-claims is arithmetically wrong. The 'buyback essentially unused' observation was published on PRNewswire on 2026-06-08 in the Q3 FY26 results release: 'As of March 31, 2026, the Company had repurchased approximately 392,000 of its Class A ordinary shares for approximately US$482,000' — $482k of a $5m authorisation, 90% unused, seven months into a twelve-month programme, in a release that was syndicated widely (TradingView, Manila Times, Grafa). The 2026-08-28 6-K adds only about 126,063 shares and $118,000 to that picture plus a one-year extension, and the tape moved +0.11% on it. Second, and more damaging: the claim that 'the company stopped buying entirely as the stock fell from ~$1.16 to a 52-week low near $0.67' is refuted by the two documents the finding itself rests on. 518,063 - 392,000 = 126,063 shares and $600,000 - $482,000 = $118,000 were bought between 2026-03-31 and 2026-08-27, at an implied average of about $0.94 — well below $1.16 and well into the decline. The '$1.16 average' is a programme-blended figure, not evidence that purchases only happened at $1.16, and the hunter uses it as if it were. Third, the direction is not established: an under-used authorisation with ~$4.4m still available against $18.3m of cash (2026-03-31) reads as retained optionality at least as easily as as a signal of managerial disbelief, and an FPI buying in size through blackout windows is constrained anyway. I concede that the specific 'expired 88% unused and was rolled unchanged' framing appears only in an EDGAR 6-K with no press release and no pickup I could find, which is why this is 78 and not 92.

findings.finding: The baseline's 20-day average volume of 405,662 shares is essentially one session: GMHS traded 7,142,358 shares on 2026-08-31 (+16.51%) with no company filing or press release on or around that date, while the surrounding sessions traded 6,192 (2026-08-13), 19,279 (2026-08-11), 22,908 (2026-08-12), 35,144 (2026-08-27) and 66,901 (2026-08-28) shares - so the true book into this print is tens of thousands of shares a day, and the +16.5% spike has already bled off across four consecutive down days to $0.77.
findings.adversary_note: This is a dispersion claim with no directional content, and I confirm both the arithmetic and the conclusion — with two qualifications. Confirmed independently from the price history: 2026-08-31 traded 7,142,358 shares at +16.51%, against 6,192 (08-13), 19,279 (08-11), 22,908 (08-12), 35,144 (08-27) and 66,901 (08-28). 7,142,358/20 = 357,118 of the baseline's 405,662 ADV, so roughly 88% of the stated ADV is one session and the true book into the print is tens of thousands of shares a day. That materially recasts the baseline's liquidity picture and is not published as an observation anywhere I could find. Two counters keep this above the 0-15 band. First, the baseline already half-contains the conclusion: realised_vol_20d of 86.6% annualised is a ~5.4% daily sigma, which by itself says the 4.19% expected move is too narrow — the dispersion insight is partly redundant with a number already sealed in the baseline, and 86.6% is itself inflated by the same 08-31 session. Second, the sub-claims are loose. 'No company filing or press release on or around that date' is contradicted by the hunter's own GMHS#2 source: a 6-K was filed Friday 2026-08-28, the session immediately before the Monday spike, disclosing the buyback extension.
